Rain Riding Survival Guide

Rain increases motorcycle accident risk by 34%. These eight tips keep you safe when the heavens open.

  1. Smooth Inputs — Gentle throttle, brakes, and steering. No sudden moves.
  2. Increase Following Distance — Double your normal gap. Braking distances double on wet roads.
  3. Avoid Road Markings — White lines, manhole covers, and painted surfaces are like ice when wet.
  4. Watch for Standing Water — Puddles hide potholes. Aquaplaning risk above 50mph.
  5. Use Both Brakes — Progressive front and rear together. Never grab the front brake.
  6. Visor Management — Pinlock insert essential. Crack visor slightly for airflow.
  7. Tyre Check — Minimum 2mm tread for wet grip.
  8. Be Visible — Spray reduces visibility massively. Use dipped headlight, hi-vis gear.
keyTakeaways: Rain increases motorcycle accident risk by around 34%.
Use smooth throttle, brake and steering inputs and double your following distance.
Avoid painted road markings, manhole covers and painted surfaces, which are like ice when wet.
Use both brakes progressively and never grab the front brake.
A Pinlock visor insert and at least 2mm of tread are essential for wet riding.

faq.q: How much more dangerous is riding in the rain?
faq.a: Rain raises motorcycle accident risk by around 34%. Wet roads cut grip, double braking distances and hide hazards like potholes under puddles. Reduced visibility from spray compounds the problem. The good news is that adjusting your technique, spacing and gear dramatically reduces the risk, so wet riding is manageable with the right approach.

faq.q: What should I avoid riding over in the wet?
faq.a: Painted road markings, manhole covers, metal drain grates and other smooth surfaces become extremely slippery in the rain, almost like ice. Try to avoid crossing them while braking or leaning, and take them upright and gently when unavoidable. Standing water is another hazard, as puddles can hide potholes and cause aquaplaning above 50mph.

faq.q: How should I brake in wet conditions?
faq.a: Use both brakes together, applying them progressively and smoothly rather than grabbing the front, which can lock the wheel and cause a slide. Brake in a straight line before corners rather than mid-bend, and increase your following distance to give yourself more room, as stopping distances roughly double on wet roads.

faq.q: How do I stop my visor fogging in the rain?
faq.a: A Pinlock insert is the most effective solution, creating a double-glazed effect that resists fogging in cool, damp conditions. Cracking the visor open slightly also improves airflow and reduces misting. Anti-fog sprays help as a backup. Clear vision is critical in the rain, so sorting fogging before you ride is well worth it.

faq.q: What tyre tread do I need for wet riding?
faq.a: You need at least 2mm of tread for reliable wet grip, more than the 1mm UK legal minimum, because deeper grooves disperse water and reduce aquaplaning. Tyres near the legal limit lose grip significantly in the rain. Check your tread and pressures before wet rides, and replace worn tyres before conditions turn against you.
